title: Constructive Specification for Plug-and-Play Learnware Agents

problem.claim: The task is to select the most suitable black-box agent for each query from a heterogeneous candidate pool.

gap.claim: Existing approaches based on costly input-output evaluation, exhaustive profiling, or router retraining are impractical at scale.

contributions.claim: A constructive specification approach builds hierarchical capability representations from limited profiling over diverse benchmarks.
An optimism-guided profiler prioritizes informative regions and prunes low-utility areas with guarantees.

A serving-time mechanism maps queries and system-maintained benchmarks into a shared specification space for multi-granularity similarity matching without accessing agent internals or training an additional selector.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments report that the approach outperforms contenders when selecting among lightweight agents.
Experiments report that the approach matches or surpasses much larger models on several tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: API-accessible, tool-augmented agents are increasingly deployed at scale in a heterogeneous and rapidly evolving ecosystem.
Query-level identification among black-box agents is difficult because exhaustive profiling and router retraining are costly at scale.
The learnware paradigm frames identification as capability-specification matching, avoiding pool-dependent retraining and exhaustive supervision.
Constructive specification uses limited profiling, optimism-guided exploration, and hierarchical capability representations.
Queries are matched in the specification space at serving time, and experiments report competitive performance against contenders and larger models.

source_observation.claim: Capability specifications can support agent identification without pool-dependent retraining or exhaustive supervision.

interpretation.claim: Separating capability representation from selector training may make black-box agent routing more adaptable as candidate pools evolve.

application.claim: A system could maintain benchmark-based capability profiles and match new queries against them at serving time.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance across domains, agent types, or deployment conditions beyond the reported tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the profiling budget, benchmarks, guarantees, or similarity-matching procedure.
The abstract does not identify the contenders, tasks, datasets, or quantitative performance results.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or failure cases.
